title: Compact Admin Cartridge: gated shortflows catalog + replayable observability
creator: Ava Patel
description: Build a lightweight, composable 'Compact Admin Cartridge' that packages common admin utilities (shortflows) into gated task artifacts that are discoverable, replayable, and instrumented. Purpose: reduce mean-time-to-resolution for oncall and first-line support by exposing vetted, permissioned micro-operations (eg. user reset, quota top-up, model restart) as task endpoints with rich telemetry. The cartridge will include: (1) a registry and metadata index for shortflows, (2) a policy gating layer that checks RBAC + approval signals before execution, (3) deterministic dry-run and replay modes wired to synthetic telemetry, and (4) minimal SDK surface for console and CLI integration. Key constraints: must be safe for private deployments (no cloud-only dependencies), support both hosted and Dedicated control planes, and emit structured telemetry compatible with Console's cost/latency dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Registry UI: list of shortflows with version, owner, and risk score
Execution API: POST /admin/v1/shortflows/:id/execute responds with execution id and events stream
Gating: executions are blocked when user lacks RBAC or when policy flags require approval
Replay/Dry-run: executions can be simulated against a sandbox and produce synthetic telemetry traces
Telemetry: events are emitted in structured form (trace_id, step, outcome, cost_tokens) and visible in Console traces
Integration tests: end-to-end smoke test against local private control plane passes
Security review: security_review_required flagged and passed before GA
progress_updates: 2026-02-26 - Kickoff meeting with PM and Design. Captured principal shortflows and initial safety heuristics. Action: inventory 12 candidate shortflows.
2026-03-03 - Prototype of registry index (Go service) completed. Exposes GET /catalog and POST /catalog/register. Initial schema includes risk_score, required_scopes, and dry_run_hint.
2026-03-07 - Design provided wireframes for the Console listing and the execution modal. Design feedback: show historical runs and a compact diff for config changes.
2026-03-10 - Implemented policy gate shim that consults IAM and a local policy engine. Added an approval hook that can route to a reviewers queue.
2026-03-12 - Security reviewed the prototype and requested explicit audit events for argument values and approvals. Added audit event plan to backlog.
2026-03-15 - QA created a harness for dry-run replay using recorded fixtures from previous incidents. Initial replay succeeded for 7/12 candidate shortflows.
2026-03-17 - Current: solid alpha internal demo scheduled for 2026-03-20 with SRE and Support. Remaining: finalize telemetry schema, implement RBAC plugin, finalize rollout plan.
decisions: Use a small JSON-first registry service (Go) rather than a full DB migration to stay portable for Private deployments
Adopt structured telemetry format aligning with Console's trace model: {trace_id, span_id, step_name, duration_ms, token_count, result_code}
Dry-run will run in a constrained sandbox that fakes external side-effects and emits synthetic cost tokens for accurate Console cost estimates
Approval gating: initial implementation will support manual approvers and an automated fallback (2-hour timeout) configurable per shortflow
Expose execution as a task endpoint with a stable API (versioned) so external automations can call shortflows as tasks
blockers: RBAC plugin integration waiting on IAM team to finalize the new group-scope mapping (ENG-???)
Telemetry schema final signoff required from Console team to ensure visibility and cost attribution
Approval queue persistence: we need a small durable queue (Kafka/SQS) decision for private deployments — product decision pending
next_steps: Finish RBAC plugin contract and prototype for Private control plane
Wire telemetry adapter into Console dev environment and validate cost attribution for synthetic runs
Complete approval-queue persistence decision and prototype durable queue for Private deployments
Schedule internal alpha demo and capture feedback for iteration
notes: Trade-offs: We intentionally keep the cartridge minimal to avoid heavy coupling with the runtime. Complex orchestration will remain in downstream runbook services.
Fallback behavior: when policy engine is unreachable, default to deny execution and surface actionable error to the caller
Rollout plan: start with internal SRE + Support groups, then expand to partner customers on Dedicated for early feedback
